sanskrit: bhūya eva mahātejā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ abravīt praśritaṃ vākyaṃ sītāpratyayakāraṇāt
english: Then that great-spirited Hanumān, son of the wind-god, spoke again with humble words, for the sake of convincing Sītā.

sanskrit: vānaro 'haṃ mahābhāge dūto rāmasya dhīmataḥ rāmanāmāṅkitaṃ cedaṃ paśya devy aṅgulīyakam samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te kṣīṇaduḥkhaphalā hy asi
english: "I am a monkey, O most fortunate lady, the envoy of the wise Rāma. Look, O goddess, at this ring inscribed with Rāma's name. Take heart; all will be well — your suffering is nearing its end."

sanskrit: gṛhītvā prekṣamāṇā sā bhartuḥ karavibhūṣaṇam bhartāram iva saṃprāptā jānakī muditābhavat
english: Taking it and gazing at that ring which had adorned her husband's hand, Jānakī rejoiced as though she had recovered her lord himself.

sanskrit: cāru tad vadanaṃ tasyās tāmraśuklāyatekṣaṇam babhūva praharṣodagraṃ rāhumukta ivoḍurāṭ
english: Her lovely face — with eyes large, flushed and white — blazed with intense joy, like the moon king freed from Rāhu.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā hrīmatī bālā bhartuḥ saṃdeśaharṣitā parituṭṣā priyaṃ śrutvā prāśaṃsata mahākapim
english: Then that modest, young woman, gladdened by her husband's message and fully satisfied on hearing the welcome news, praised the great monkey.

sanskrit: vikrāntas tvaṃ samarthas tvaṃ prājñas tvaṃ vānarottama yenedaṃ rākṣasapadaṃ tvayaikena pradharṣitam
english: "You are brave, you are capable, you are wise, O best of monkeys — you alone have dared to enter this realm of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: śatayojanavistīrṇaḥ sāgaro makarālayaḥ vikramaślāghanīyena kramatā goṣpadīkṛtaḥ
english: "The ocean, a hundred yojanas wide, the abode of sea-monsters, was made a mere cow's hoof-print by your praiseworthy stride."

sanskrit: na hi tvāṃ prākṛtaṃ manye vanaraṃ vanararṣabha yasya te nāsti saṃtrāso rāvaṇān nāpi saṃbhramaḥ
english: "I do not think you an ordinary monkey, O bull among monkeys, for you feel no terror or agitation before Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: arhase ca kapiśreṣṭha mayā samabhibhāṣitum yady asi preṣitas tena rāmeṇa viditātmanā
english: "You deserve to be addressed by me, O best of monkeys, if you are truly sent by that Rāma who knows the self."

sanskrit: preṣayiṣyati durdharṣo rāmo na hy aparīkṣitam parākramam avijñāya matsakāśaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: "The invincible Rāma would not send one whose valor is untested and unknown, especially to come to me."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā ca kuśalī rāmo dharmātmā dharmavatsalaḥ lakṣmaṇaś ca mahātejāḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ
english: "By good fortune, Rāma the righteous-souled, devoted to dharma, is well; and the great-spirited Lakṣmaṇa, who increases the joy of Sumitrā, is well."

sanskrit: kuśalī yadi kākutsthaḥ kiṃ nu sāgaramekhalām mahīṃ dahati kopena yugāntāgnir ivotthitaḥ
english: "If Kākutstha is well, why then does he not burn the ocean-girdled earth with his wrath, blazing like the fire at the world's end?"

sanskrit: atha vā śaktimantau tau surāṇām api nigrahe mamaiva tu na duḥkhānām asti manye viparyayaḥ
english: "Or perhaps those two are capable even of subduing the gods, yet I think there is no reversal of my own sorrows."

sanskrit: kaccic ca vyathate rāmaḥ kaccin na paripatyate uttarāṇi ca kāryāṇi kurute puruṣottamaḥ
english: "Does Rāma grieve? Does he not wander distracted? Does that best of men attend to the tasks that lie ahead?"

sanskrit: kaccin na dīnaḥ saṃbhrāntaḥ kāryeṣu ca na muhyati kaccin puruṣakāryāṇi kurute nṛpateḥ sutaḥ
english: "Is he not wretched, not bewildered? Does he not lose himself amid his duties? Does that son of a king perform the deeds a man must do?"

sanskrit: dvividhaṃ trividhopāyam upāyam api sevate vijigīṣuḥ suhṛt kaccin mitreṣu ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: "Does that scorcher of foes, desiring victory, employ the two-fold and three-fold strategies, and maintain bonds of friendship?"

sanskrit: kaccin mitrāṇi labhate mitraiś cāpy abhigamyate kaccit kalyāṇamitraś ca mitraiś cāpi puraskṛtaḥ
english: "Does he secure allies and are his allies approaching him? Does he keep good company and is he honored by his friends?"

sanskrit: kaccid āśāsti devānāṃ prasādaṃ pārthivātmajaḥ kaccit puruṣakāraṃ ca daivaṃ ca pratipadyate
english: "Does that son of a king seek the grace of the gods? Does he rely on both human effort and divine fate?"

sanskrit: kaccin na vigatasneho vivāsān mayi rāghavaḥ kaccin māṃ vyasanād asmān mokṣayiṣyati vānaraḥ
english: "Has Rāghava's love for me not faded on account of my absence? Will the monkey-hero deliver me from this calamity?"

sanskrit: sukhānām ucito nityaṃ asukhānām anūcitaḥ duḥkham uttaram āsādya kaccid rāmo na sīdati
english: "Ever accustomed to happiness and unaccustomed to misery, has Rāma, encountering this great sorrow, not fallen into despair?"

sanskrit: kausalyāyās tathā kaccit sumitrāyās tathaiva ca abhīkṣṇaṃ śrūyate kaccit kuśalaṃ bharatasya ca
english: "And what of Kausalyā? What of Sumitrā likewise? Is tidings of Bharata's welfare regularly heard?"

sanskrit: mannimittena mānārhaḥ kaccic chokena rāghavaḥ kaccin nānyamanā rāmaḥ kaccin māṃ tārayiṣyati
english: "Is Rāghava, who deserves all honor, consumed by grief on my account? Is Rāma's mind not elsewhere? Will he save me?"

sanskrit: kaccid akṣauhiṇīṃ bhīmāṃ bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ dhvajinīṃ mantribhir guptāṃ preṣayiṣyati matkṛte
english: "Will Bharata, devoted to his brothers, send a terrible army with its banners, protected by ministers, for my sake?"

sanskrit: vānarādhipatiḥ śrīmān sugrīvaḥ kaccid eṣyati matkṛte haribhir vīrair vṛto dantanakhāyudhaiḥ
english: "Will Sugrīva, the glorious lord of the monkeys, come for my sake, surrounded by brave monkeys armed with teeth and claws?"

sanskrit: kaccic ca lakṣmaṇaḥ śūraḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ astravic charajālena rākṣasān vidhamiṣyati
english: "Will the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, who increases the joy of Sumitrā, the knower of weapons, scatter the rākṣasas with his net of arrows?"

sanskrit: raudreṇa kaccid astreṇa rāmeṇa nihataṃ raṇe drakṣyāmy alpena kālena rāvaṇaṃ sasuhṛjjanam
english: "Will I see, before long, Rāvaṇa and all his kinsmen slain in battle by Rāma with his terrible weapon?"

sanskrit: kaccin na tad dhemasamānavarṇaṃ tasyānanaṃ padmasamānagandhi mayā vinā śuṣyati śokadīnaṃ jalakṣaye padmam ivātapena
english: "Does not that face of his, golden in hue, fragrant as a lotus, wither with grief in my absence, like a lotus withered by the sun when the water dries?"

sanskrit: dharmāpadeśāt tyajataś ca rājyāṃ māṃ cāpy araṇyaṃ nayataḥ padātim nāsīd vyathā yasya na bhīr na śokaḥ kaccit sa dhairyaṃ hṛdaye karoti
english: "He who felt no anguish, no fear, no grief when he renounced his kingdom under pretext of duty and led me on foot into the forest — does that one hold steadiness in his heart?"

sanskrit: na cāsya mātā na pitā na cānyaḥ snehād viśiṣṭo 'sti mayā samo vā tāvad dhy ahaṃ dūtajijīviṣeyaṃ yāvat pravṛttiṃ śṛṇuyāṃ priyasya
english: "Neither his mother, nor his father, nor any other holds a love surpassing or equal to mine for him. I shall live only so long, like a messenger, as I can hear tidings of my beloved."

sanskrit: itīva devī vacanaṃ mahārthaṃ taṃ vānarendraṃ madhurārtham uktvā śrotuṃ punas tasya vaco 'bhirāmaṃ rāmārthayuktaṃ virarāma rāmā
english: Having thus spoken to that lord of monkeys words weighty and sweet in meaning, Rāmā — Sītā — fell silent, longing to hear again his delightful words full of tidings about Rāma.

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā mārutir bhīmavikramaḥ śirasy añjalim ādhāya vākyam uttaram abravīt
english: Having heard Sītā's words, the son of the wind-god, of fearsome prowess, placed his joined palms upon his head and spoke in reply.

sanskrit: na tvām ihasthāṃ jānīte rāmaḥ kamalalocanaḥ śrutvaiva tu vaco mahyaṃ kṣipram eṣyati rāghavaḥ
english: "Lotus-eyed Rāma does not know that you are here. But upon hearing my report, Rāghava will come swiftly."

sanskrit: camūṃ prakarṣan mahatīṃ haryṛṣkagaṇasaṃkulām viṣṭambhayitvā bāṇaughair akṣobhyaṃ varuṇālayam kariṣyati purīṃ laṅkāṃ kākutsthaḥ śāntarākṣasām
english: "Leading his great army swarming with monkeys and bears, Kākutstha will pin down the ocean — the abode of Varuṇa, that which cannot be disturbed — with torrents of arrows, and will make this city of Laṅkā free of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tatra yady antarā mṛtyur yadi devāḥ sahāsurāḥ sthāsyanti pathi rāmasya sa tān api vadhiṣyati
english: "If Death itself, if the gods together with the asuras, should stand in Rāma's path, he will slay them too."

sanskrit: tavādarśanajenārye śokena sa pariplutaḥ na śarma labhate rāmaḥ siṃhārdita iva dvipaḥ
english: "Flooded with the grief born of not seeing you, O noble lady, Rāma finds no peace, like an elephant tormented by a lion."

sanskrit: dardareṇa ca te devi śape mūlaphalena ca malayena ca vindhyena meruṇā mandareṇa ca
english: "By the Dardara mountain, O goddess, I swear to you, and by roots and fruits, by Malaya, Vindhya, Meru, and Mandara."

sanskrit: yathā sunayanaṃ valgu bimbauṣṭhaṃ cārukuṇḍalam mukhaṃ drakṣyasi rāmasya pūrṇacandram ivoditam
english: "As surely as you shall behold Rāma's face — beautiful-eyed, lovely, with lips red as the bimba fruit, adorned with fair earrings, risen like the full moon."

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi vaidehi rāmaṃ prasravaṇe girau śatakratum ivāsīnaṃ nākapṛṣṭhasya mūrdhani
english: "You will soon see Rāma, O Vaidehi, on Mount Prasravaṇa, seated like Indra of a hundred sacrifices on the summit of heaven."

sanskrit: na māṃsaṃ rāghavo bhuṅkte na cāpi madhusevate vanyaṃ suvihitaṃ nityaṃ bhaktam aśnāti pañcamam
english: "Rāghava eats no meat and takes no honey; he eats only forest food, properly prepared, at the fifth hour."

sanskrit: naiva daṃśān na maśakān na kīṭān na sarīsṛpān rāghavo 'panayed gatrāt tvadgatenāntarātmanā
english: "Rāghava does not remove from his body the biting flies, the mosquitoes, the insects, or the crawling creatures, his inmost self entirely absorbed in you."

sanskrit: nityaṃ dhyānaparo rāmo nityaṃ śokaparāyaṇaḥ nānyac cintayate kiṃ cit sa tu kāmavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: "Rāma is ever given to meditation, ever overwhelmed with grief; he thinks of nothing else — he is utterly subject to his longing."

sanskrit: anidraḥ satataṃ rāmaḥ supto 'pi ca narottamaḥ sīteti madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ vyāharan pratibudhyate
english: "Rāma is ever sleepless; even that best of men, when he does sleep, wakes uttering the sweet syllables 'Sītā'."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā phalaṃ vā puṣpaṃ vā yac cānyat strīmanoharam bahuśo hā priyety evaṃ śvasaṃs tvām abhibhāṣate
english: "On seeing a fruit or a flower or anything else that would delight a woman, he sighs again and again and speaks as if to you: 'Ah, my beloved!'"

sanskrit: sa devi nityaṃ paritapyamānas tvām eva sītety abhibhāṣamāṇaḥ dhṛtavrato rājasuto mahātmā tavaiva lābhāya kṛtaprayatnaḥ
english: "He, O goddess, ever burning in anguish, ever calling out your name 'Sītā', that great-souled prince firm in his vow, makes every effort solely for the sake of winning you back."

sanskrit: sā rāmasaṃkīrtanavītaśokā rāmasya śokena samānaśokā śaranmukhenāmbudaśeṣacandrā niśeva vaidehasutā babhūva
english: She, the daughter of Videha, her grief dispersed by the recounting of Rāma's virtues yet equal to Rāma's own grief in sorrow, became like the night at the close of autumn with its moon breaking through the last of the clouds.

sanskrit: sītā tad vacanaṃ śrutvā pūrṇacandranibhānanā hanūmantam uvācedaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Sītā, her face like the full moon, having heard those words, spoke thus to Hanumān — words joined with righteousness and meaning.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ viṣasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ tvayā vānarabhāṣitam yac ca nānyamanā rāmo yac ca śokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: "What you, O monkey, have spoken is nectar mixed with poison: that Rāma's mind is not elsewhere — and yet that he is sunk in grief."

sanskrit: aiśvarye vā suvistīrṇe vyasane vā sudāruṇe rajjveva puruṣaṃ baddhvā kṛtāntaḥ parikarṣati
english: "Whether in the vastness of prosperity or in the most terrible adversity, fate drags a man about like one bound by a rope."

sanskrit: vidhir nūnam asaṃhāryaḥ prāṇināṃ plavagottama saumitriṃ māṃ ca rāmaṃ ca vyasanaiḥ paśya mohitān
english: "Fate for living beings is surely irresistible, O best of monkeys — behold Saumitrī, and me, and Rāma, all bewildered by calamities."

sanskrit: śokasyāsya kadā pāraṃ rāghavo 'dhigamiṣyati plavamānaḥ pariśrānto hatanauḥ sāgare yathā
english: "When will Rāghava reach the far shore of this sorrow, like one exhausted from swimming, whose boat has been wrecked in the ocean?"

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ kṣayaṃ kṛtvā sūdayitvā ca rāvaṇam laṅkām unmūlitāṃ kṛtvā kadā drakṣyati māṃ patiḥ
english: "When will my lord, having destroyed the rākṣasas, having slain Rāvaṇa, having uprooted Laṅkā, come to see me?"

sanskrit: sa vācyaḥ saṃtvarasveti yāvad eva na pūryate ayaṃ saṃvatsaraḥ kālas tāvad dhi mama jīvitam
english: "He is to be told: 'Make haste' — for as long as this year is not completed, only so long is my life."

sanskrit: vartate daśamo māso dvau tu śeṣau plavaṃgama rāvaṇena nṛśaṃsena samayo yaḥ kṛto mama
english: "The tenth month has come; two remain, O monkey. Such was the term set for me by the cruel Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇena ca bhrātrā mama niryātanaṃ prati anunītaḥ prayatnena na ca tat kurute matim
english: "His brother Vibhīṣaṇa has earnestly beseeched him to restore me, yet Rāvaṇa will not set his mind to it."

sanskrit: mama pratipradānaṃ hi rāvaṇasya na rocate rāvaṇaṃ mārgate saṃkhye mṛtyuḥ kālavaśaṃ gatam
english: "Returning me does not please Rāvaṇa — death, subject to time, seeks Rāvaṇa in battle."

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhā kanyānalā nama vibhīṣaṇasutā kape tayā mamaitad ākhyātaṃ mātrā prahitayā svayam
english: "The eldest daughter of Vibhīṣaṇa, named Analā, O monkey, was sent by her own mother, and it is she who disclosed this to me."

sanskrit: avindhyo nāma medhāvī vidvān rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ dhṛtimāñ śīlavān vṛddho rāvaṇasya susaṃmataḥ
english: "There is a wise and learned bull among rākṣasas named Avindhya, steadfast and virtuous, aged, and greatly honored by Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: rāmāt kṣayam anuprāptaṃ rakṣasāṃ pratyacodayat na ca tasyāpi duṣṭātmā śṛṇoti vacanaṃ hitam
english: "He urged Rāvaṇa that the destruction of the rākṣasas would come from Rāma, yet that corrupt-souled one does not listen to even his beneficial counsel."

sanskrit: āśaṃseti hariśreṣṭha kṣipraṃ māṃ prāpsyate patiḥ antarātmā hi me śuddhas tasmiṃś ca bahavo guṇāḥ
english: "I have hope, O best of monkeys: my lord will reach me soon. My inner self is pure, and in him there are many virtues."

sanskrit: utsāhaḥ pauruṣaṃ sattvam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṛtajñatā vikramaś ca prabhāvaś ca santi vānararāghave
english: "Energy, manhood, valor, compassion, gratitude, heroism, and might — these dwell in the monkey-lord and in Rāghava."

sanskrit: caturdaśasahasrāṇi rākṣasānāṃ jaghāna yaḥ janasthāne vinā bhrātrā śatruḥ kas tasya nodvijet
english: "He who slew fourteen thousand rākṣasas at Janasthāna without a brother at his side — what enemy would not tremble before him?"

sanskrit: na sa śakyas tulayituṃ vyasanaiḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ ahaṃ tasyānubhāvajñā śakrasyeva pulomajā
english: "That bull among men cannot be measured by calamities. I know his glory, as Pulomā's daughter knows that of Indra."

sanskrit: śarajālāṃśumāñ śūraḥ kape rāmadivākaraḥ śatrurakṣomayaṃ toyam upaśoṣaṃ nayiṣyati
english: "The heroic sun that is Rāma, O monkey, with its rays of arrow-nets, will dry up the water that is filled with the filth of enemies and rākṣasas."

sanskrit: iti saṃjalpamānāṃ tāṃ rāmārthe śokakarśitām aśrusaṃpūrṇavadanām uvāca hanumān kapiḥ
english: As she thus spoke on, emaciated by grief for Rāma's sake, her face filled with tears, the monkey Hanumān addressed her.

sanskrit: śrutvaiva tu vaco mahyaṃ kṣipram eṣyati rāghavaḥ camūṃ prakarṣan mahatīṃ haryṛkṣagaṇasaṃkulām
english: "Upon hearing my report, Rāghava will come swiftly, leading his great army swarming with troops of monkeys and bears."

sanskrit: atha vā mocayiṣyāmi tām adyaiva hi rākṣasāt asmād duḥkhād upāroha mama pṛṣṭham anindite
english: "Or else I will free you this very day from the rākṣasa and from this sorrow. Climb upon my back, O blameless one."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi pṛṣṭhagatāṃ kṛtvā saṃtariṣyāmi sāgaram śaktir asti hi me voḍhuṃ laṅkām api sarāvaṇām
english: "With you seated on my back I shall cross the ocean; I have the strength to carry even all of Laṅkā with Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: ahaṃ prasravaṇasthāya rāghavāyādya maithili prāpayiṣyāmi śakrāya havyaṃ hutam ivānalaḥ
english: "I shall deliver you today, O Maithilī, to Rāghava dwelling on Mount Prasravaṇa, as fire delivers the oblation to Indra."

sanskrit: drakṣyasy adyaiva vaidehi rāghavaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam vyavasāya samāyuktaṃ viṣṇuṃ daityavadhe yathā
english: "You will see this very day, O Vaidehi, Rāghava together with Lakṣmaṇa, fully resolved for action, like Viṣṇu set upon the slaying of the daityas."

sanskrit: tvaddarśanakṛtotsāham āśramasthaṃ mahābalam puraṃdaram ivāsīnaṃ nāgarājasya mūrdhani
english: "Fired with zeal by the sight of you, mighty, stationed at the hermitage, seated like Purandara upon the head of the king of serpents."

sanskrit: pṛṣṭham āroha me devi mā vikāṅkṣasva śobhane yogam anviccha rāmeṇa śaśāṅkeneva rohiṇī
english: "Mount my back, O goddess; do not hesitate, O beautiful one. Seek your union with Rāma as Rohiṇī seeks the moon."

sanskrit: kathayantīva candreṇa sūryeṇeva suvarcalā matpṛṣṭham adhiruhya tvaṃ tarākāśamahārṇavam
english: "Like one who speaks with the moon, like Suvarcalā with the sun — mounting my back, you shall cross the great sky-ocean of stars."

sanskrit: na hi me saṃprayātasya tvām ito nayato 'ṅgane anugantuṃ gatiṃ śaktāḥ sarve laṅkānivāsinaḥ
english: "For when I set forth taking you away from here, O lady, not all the inhabitants of Laṅkā are capable of following my course."

sanskrit: yathaivāham iha prāptas tathaivāham asaṃśayam yāsyāmi paśya vaidehi tvām udyamya vihāyasaṃ
english: "Just as I arrived here, so without doubt shall I depart — see, O Vaidehi, I will lift you and go through the sky."

sanskrit: maithilī tu hariśreṣṭhāc chrutvā vacanam adbhutam harṣavismitasarvāṅgī hanūmantam athābravīt
english: Maithilī, having heard from that best of monkeys these astonishing words, her every limb thrilled with wonder and joy, then spoke to Hanumān.

sanskrit: hanūman dūram adhvanaṃ kathaṃ māṃ voḍhum icchasi tad eva khalu te manye kapitvaṃ hariyūthapa
english: "Hanumān, how do you wish to carry me on the long journey? That, I think, is indeed your monkey-nature, O leader of monkey-troops."

sanskrit: kathaṃ vālpaśarīras tvaṃ mām ito netum icchasi sakāśaṃ mānavendrasya bhartur me plavagarṣabha
english: "How can you, with so small a body, wish to take me from here to the presence of the lord of the monkey-host, my husband, O bull among monkeys?"

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ cintayām āsa lakṣmīvān navaṃ paribhavaṃ kṛtam
english: Hearing Sītā's words, the glorious Hanumān, son of the wind-god, reflected — a fresh slight had been given to him.

sanskrit: na me jānāti sattvaṃ vā prabhāvaṃ vāsitekṣaṇā tasmāt paśyatu vaidehī yad rūpaṃ mama kāmataḥ
english: "The dark-eyed one does not know my strength or my power; therefore let Vaidehi see whatever form of mine I choose."

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya hanumāṃs tadā plavagasattamaḥ darśayām āsa vaidehyāḥ svarūpam arimardanaḥ
english: Having reflected thus, that best of monkeys, the crusher of foes Hanumān, thereupon revealed his true form to Vaidehi.

sanskrit: sa tasmāt pādapād dhīmān āplutya plavagarṣabhaḥ tato vardhitum ārebhe sītāpratyayakāraṇāt
english: That wise bull among monkeys leaped down from that tree and then began to grow in size, for the sake of convincing Sītā.

sanskrit: merumandārasaṃkāśo babhau dīptānalaprabhaḥ agrato vyavatasthe ca sītāyā vānararṣabhaḥ
english: Like Meru or Mandara in appearance, blazing with the radiance of a bright fire, that bull among monkeys stood before Sītā.

sanskrit: hariḥ parvatasaṃkāśas tāmravaktro mahābalaḥ vajradaṃṣṭranakho bhīmo vaidehīm idam abravīt
english: That monkey, mountain-like, with a copper-red face, of great strength, his teeth and claws hard as thunderbolts, terrible, spoke these words to Vaidehi.

sanskrit: saparvatavanoddeśāṃ sāṭṭaprākāratoraṇām laṅkām imāṃ sanathāṃ vā nayituṃ śaktir asti me
english: "I have the power to carry away this very Laṅkā, with its tracts of forest and mountains, with its towers and walls and gateways, together with its lord."

sanskrit: tad avasthāpya tāṃ buddhir alaṃ devi vikāṅkṣayā viśokaṃ kuru vaidehi rāghavaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam
english: "Therefore abandon that thought; enough of doubt, O goddess. Make Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa free from sorrow, O Vaidehi."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvācalasaṃkāśam uvāca janakātmajā padmapatraviśālākṣī mārutasyaurasaṃ sutam
english: Seeing him, mountain-like, Janaka's daughter, she of wide lotus-petal eyes, spoke to the true-born son of the wind-god.

sanskrit: tava sattvaṃ balaṃ caiva vijānāmi mahākape vāyor iva gatiṃ cāpi tejaś cāgnir ivādbhutam
english: "I know your valor and your strength, O great monkey; your speed is like the wind's, your energy wonderful as fire's."

sanskrit: prākṛto 'nyaḥ kathaṃ cemāṃ bhūmim āgantum arhati udadher aprameyasya pāraṃ vānarapuṃgava
english: "How could any ordinary being deserve to cross to the far shore of this immeasurable ocean and come to this land, O bull among monkeys?"

sanskrit: jānāmi gamane śaktiṃ nayane cāpi te mama avaśyaṃ sāmpradhāryāśu kāryasiddhir ihātmanaḥ
english: "I know your power in going and in bringing me; the success of our enterprise here must be quickly considered."

sanskrit: ayuktaṃ tu kapiśreṣṭha mayā gantuṃ tvayā saha vāyuvegasavegasya vego māṃ mohayet tava
english: "Yet it would be improper for me to go with you, O best of monkeys; the speed of your speed — swift as the wind — would bewilder me."

sanskrit: aham ākāśam āsaktā upary upari sāgaram prapateyaṃ hi te pṛṣṭhād bhayād vegena gacchataḥ
english: "Suspended in the sky, above the ocean, I would fall from your back out of fear as you go with speed."

sanskrit: patitā sāgare cāhaṃ timinakrajhaṣākule bhayeyam āśu vivaśā yādasām annam uttamam
english: "Fallen into the ocean, teeming with timi-fish, sharks, and great sea-creatures, helpless, I would quickly become the choicest meal of the denizens of the deep."

sanskrit: na ca śakṣye tvayā sārdhaṃ gantuṃ śatruvināśana kalatravati saṃdehas tvayy api syād asaṃśayam
english: "And I cannot go together with you, O destroyer of foes; even in you, who have a wife, doubt would arise, without question."

sanskrit: hriyamāṇāṃ tu māṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ anugaccheyur ādiṣṭā rāvaṇena durātmanā
english: "Seeing me being carried away, the rākṣasas of fearsome prowess, dispatched by the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, would pursue us."

sanskrit: tais tvaṃ parivṛtaḥ śūraiḥ śūlam udgara pāṇibhiḥ bhaves tvaṃ saṃśayaṃ prāpto mayā vīra kalatravān
english: "Surrounded by those warriors brandishing spears in their hands, you — a hero with a wife to protect — would be placed in peril on my account."

sanskrit: sāyudhā bahavo vyomni rākṣasās tvaṃ nirāyudhaḥ kathaṃ śakṣyasi saṃyātuṃ māṃ caiva parirakṣitum
english: "The many rākṣasas are armed, in the sky, while you are without weapons — how will you be able to fight and protect me at the same time?"

sanskrit: yudhyamānasya rakṣobhis tatas taiḥ krūrakarmabhiḥ prapateyaṃ hi te pṛṣṭhad bhayārtā kapisattama
english: "While you fight those cruel-acting rākṣasas, I, overcome with fear, would fall from your back, O best of monkeys."

sanskrit: atha rakṣāṃsi bhīmāni mahānti balavanti ca kathaṃ cit sāmparāye tvāṃ jayeyuḥ kapisattama
english: "Or if those fearsome, great, and powerful rākṣasas should by some chance overcome you in combat, O best of monkeys —"

sanskrit: atha vā yudhyamānasya pateyaṃ vimukhasya te patitāṃ ca gṛhītvā māṃ nayeyuḥ pāparākṣasāḥ
english: "— or as you fight, your back turned away, I might fall; and having seized me fallen, the wicked rākṣasas would carry me off."

sanskrit: māṃ vā hareyus tvaddhastād viśaseyur athāpi vā avyavasthau hi dṛśyete yuddhe jayaparājayau
english: "They might snatch me from your grasp or even kill me — for victory and defeat in battle are seen to be inconstant."

sanskrit: ahaṃ vāpi vipadyeyaṃ rakṣobhir abhitarjitā tvatprayatno hariśreṣṭha bhaven niṣphala eva tu
english: "Or I might perish, terrorized by the rākṣasas; your effort, O best of monkeys, would then be entirely fruitless."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tvam api paryāpto nihantuṃ sarvarākṣasān rāghavasya yaśo hīyet tvayā śastais tu rākṣasaiḥ
english: "You may well be capable of slaying all the rākṣasas, but Rāghava's glory would be diminished if the rākṣasas were slain by you."

sanskrit: atha vādāya rakṣāṃsi nyasyeyuḥ saṃvṛte hi mām yatra te nābhijānīyur harayo nāpi rāghavaḥ
english: "Or the rākṣasas might take me away and conceal me in a hidden place where neither the monkeys nor Rāghava could find me."

sanskrit: ārambhas tu madartho 'yaṃ tatas tava nirarthakaḥ tvayā hi saha rāmasya mahān āgamane guṇaḥ
english: "This undertaking on my behalf would thus be rendered meaningless for you; but great is the merit in Rāma himself coming with you."

sanskrit: mayi jīvitam āyattaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ bhrātṝṇāṃ ca mahābāho tava rājakulasya ca
english: "On my survival depends the life of the great-souled Rāghava, of his brothers, O mighty-armed one, of you, and of the royal lineage."

sanskrit: tau nirāśau madarthe tu śokasaṃtāpakarśitau saha sarvarkṣaharibhis tyakṣyataḥ prāṇasaṃgraham
english: "Those two, despairing of me, emaciated by the burning of grief, together with all the bears and monkeys, would give up their hold on life."

sanskrit: bhartur bhaktiṃ puraskṛtya rāmād anyasya vānara nāhaṃ spraṣṭuṃ padā gātram iccheyaṃ vānarottama
english: "Putting my devotion to my husband foremost, O monkey, I would not wish the touch of any man's body but Rāma's, O best of monkeys."

sanskrit: yad ahaṃ gātrasaṃsparśaṃ rāvaṇasya gatā balāt anīśā kiṃ kariṣyāmi vināthā vivaśā satī
english: "As for Rāvaṇa's touch of my body — that was by force; what could I do, being powerless, without a protector, helpless?"

sanskrit: yadi rāmo daśagrīvam iha hatvā sarākṣasaṃ mām ito gṛhya gaccheta tat tasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet
english: "If Rāma were to slay the ten-headed one here, together with all the rākṣasas, and then take me from this place — that would be fitting for him."

sanskrit: śrutā hi dṛṣṭāś ca mayā parākramā mahātmanas tasya raṇāvamardinaḥ na devagandharvabhujaṃgarākṣasā bhavanti rāmeṇa samā hi saṃyuge
english: "I have heard of and seen the feats of valor of that great-souled crusher of foes — neither gods, gandharvas, serpents, nor rākṣasas are equal to Rāma in battle."

sanskrit: samīkṣya taṃ saṃyati citrakārmukaṃ mahābalaṃ vāsavatulyavikramam salakṣmaṇaṃ ko viṣaheta rāghavaṃ hutāśanaṃ dīptam ivānileritam
english: "Who, seeing in battle that Rāghava of great strength, wielder of the beautiful bow, equal in valor to Vāsava, together with Lakṣmaṇa — who could endure him, blazing like fire fanned by wind?"

sanskrit: salakṣmaṇaṃ rāghavam ājimardanaṃ diśāgajaṃ mattam iva vyavasthitam saheta ko vānaramukhya saṃyuge yugāntasūryapratimaṃ śarārciṣam
english: "Who could endure in battle, O chief of monkeys, Rāghava with Lakṣmaṇa, the crusher of foes, standing like a maddened elephant of the quarters, his arrows blazing like the sun at the world's end?"

sanskrit: sa me hariśreṣṭha salakṣmaṇaṃ patiṃ sayūthapaṃ kṣipram ihopapādaya cirāya rāmaṃ prati śokakarśitāṃ kuruṣva māṃ vānaramukhya harṣitām
english: "Therefore, O best of monkeys, bring my lord here quickly, together with Lakṣmaṇa and the monkey-chiefs; O chief of monkeys, make me who have long been emaciated by grief rejoice."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kapiśārdūlas tena vākyena harṣitaḥ sītām uvāca tac chrutvā vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Then that tiger among monkeys, gladdened by those words, having heard them, spoke to Sītā — he who was skilled in speech.

sanskrit: yuktarūpaṃ tvayā devi bhāṣitaṃ śubhadarśane sadṛśaṃ strīsvabhāvasya sādhvīnāṃ vinayasya ca
english: "What you have spoken, O goddess of auspicious appearance, is fitting — befitting the nature of women and the modesty of virtuous women."

sanskrit: strītvaṃ na tu samarthaṃ hi sāgaraṃ vyativartitum mām adhiṣṭhāya vistīrṇaṃ śatayojanam āyatam
english: "Womankind is indeed not capable of crossing the vast ocean, a hundred yojanas in extent, riding upon me."

sanskrit: dvitīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ yac ca bravīṣi vinayānvite rāmād anyasya nārhāmi saṃsparśam iti jānaki
english: "And the second reason you give, O lady endowed with modesty — 'I do not deserve the touch of any man but Rāma' — this is indeed true, O Jānaki."

sanskrit: etat te devi sadṛśaṃ patnyās tasya mahātmanaḥ kā hy anyā tvām ṛte devi brūyād vacanam īdṛśam
english: "This is fitting, O goddess, for the wife of that great-souled one. For who other than you, O goddess, would speak such words?"

sanskrit: śroṣyate caiva kākutsthaḥ sarvaṃ niravaśeṣataḥ ceṣṭitaṃ yat tvayā devi bhāṣitaṃ mama cāgrataḥ
english: "And Kākutstha shall hear everything without remainder — all that you have done, O goddess, and all that you have spoken before me."

sanskrit: kāraṇair bahubhir devi rāma priyacikīrṣayā snehapraskannamanasā mayaitat samudīritam
english: "For many reasons, O goddess, out of my desire to do what is dear to Rāma, with a heart overflowing with affection, I spoke this to you."

sanskrit: laṅkāyā duṣpraveśatvād dustaratvān mahodadheḥ sāmarthyād ātmanaś caiva mayaitat samudāhṛtam
english: "Because of the difficulty of entering Laṅkā, the uncrossability of the great ocean, and my own ability — this is why I proposed it."

sanskrit: icchāmi tvāṃ samānetum adyaiva raghubandhunā gurusnehena bhaktyā ca nānyathā tad udāhṛtam
english: "I wish to bring you to the kinsman of Raghu's line this very day, out of deep affection and devotion — not otherwise was that proposed."

sanskrit: yadi notsahase yātuṃ mayā sārdham anindite abhijñānaṃ prayaccha tvaṃ jānīyād rāghavo hi yat
english: "But if you are not willing to go with me, O blameless one, then give me a token of recognition by which Rāghava may know."

sanskrit: evam uktā hanumatā sītā surasutopamā uvāca vacanaṃ mandaṃ bāṣpapragrathitākṣaram
english: Addressed thus by Hanumān, Sītā — equal to a daughter of the gods — spoke slowly, her syllables strung with tears.

sanskrit: idaṃ śreṣṭham abhijñānaṃ brūyās tvaṃ tu mama priyam śailasya citrakūṭasya pāde pūrvottare tadā
english: "This is the best token of recognition; speak it to my beloved: at the northeastern foot of Mount Citrakūṭa —

sanskrit: tāpasāśramavāsinyāḥ prājyamūlaphalodake tasmin siddhāśrame deśe mandākinyā adūrataḥ
english: "— where one who dwells in the ascetic hermitage is provided with abundant roots, fruits, and water, in that place of accomplished sages, not far from the Mandākinī river —

sanskrit: tasyopavanaṣaṇḍeṣu nānāpuṣpasugandhiṣu vihṛtya salilaklinnā tavāṅke samupāviśam
english: "— in the groves of that place, fragrant with manifold flowers, having bathed and played in the water, wet with water I sat in your lap."

sanskrit: paryāyeṇa prasuptaś ca mamāṅke bharatāgrajaḥ
english: "And the elder brother of Bharata — you — fell asleep in my lap in turn."

sanskrit: tato māṃsasamāyukto vāyasaḥ paryatuṇḍayat tam ahaṃ loṣṭam udyamya vārayāmi sma vāyasaṃ
english: "Then a crow, eager for flesh, pecked at me with its beak; I took up a clod of earth to drive away that crow."

sanskrit: dārayan sa ca māṃ kākas tatraiva parilīyate na cāpy uparaman māṃsād bhakṣārthī balibhojanaḥ
english: "The crow wounded me and hid in that very place, and even so did not cease from the flesh — that eater of offerings, craving food."

sanskrit: utkarṣantyāṃ ca raśanāṃ kruddhāyāṃ mayi pakṣiṇe sraṃsamāne ca vasane tato dṛṣṭā tvayā hy aham
english: "As I was pulling at the cord of my garment, angry at the bird, my robe slipping off — you saw me in that state."

sanskrit: tvayā vihasitā cāhaṃ kruddhā saṃlajjitā tadā bhakṣya gṛddhena kālena dāritā tvām upāgatā
english: "You laughed at me; I was angry, ashamed; wounded by that crow greedy for flesh, I approached you."

sanskrit: āsīnasya ca te śrāntā punar utsaṅgam āviśam krudhyantī ca prahṛṣṭena tvayāhaṃ parisāntvitā
english: "Exhausted, I entered your lap again as you sat there; even as I was still angry, you consoled me with delight."

sanskrit: bāṣpapūrṇamukhī mandaṃ cakṣuṣī parimārjatī lakṣitāhaṃ tvayā nātha vāyasena prakopitā
english: "My face filled with tears, slowly wiping my eyes, I was noticed by you, my lord, provoked by the crow."

sanskrit: āśīviṣa iva kruddhaḥ śvasān vākyam abhāṣathāḥ kena te nāganāsoru vikṣataṃ vai stanāntaram kaḥ krīḍati saroṣeṇa pañcavaktreṇa bhoginā
english: "Hissing like an angry serpent, you spoke: 'Who has wounded the space between your breasts, O you of elephant-trunk-shaped thighs? Who plays with a five-hooded, wrathful serpent?'"

sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇas tatas taṃ vai vāyasaṃ samavaikṣathāḥ nakhaiḥ sarudhirais tīkṣṇair mām evābhimukhaṃ sthitam
english: "Then looking about, you beheld that crow — its sharp talons bloodied — standing right before me."

sanskrit: putraḥ kila sa śakrasya vāyasaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ dharāntaracaraḥ śīghraṃ pavanasya gatau samaḥ
english: "That crow is said to be the son of Indra, the best of birds, a rover of the earth's interior, equal in speed to the wind."

sanskrit: tatas tasmin mahābāhuḥ kopasaṃvartitekṣaṇaḥ vāyase kṛtavān krūrāṃ matiṃ matimatāṃ vara
english: "Then upon that crow, O best among the wise, the mighty-armed one — his eyes rolling with anger — set a cruel intent."

sanskrit: sa darbhasaṃstarād gṛhya brahmaṇo 'streṇa yojayaḥ sa dīpta iva kālāgnir jajvālābhimukho dvijam
english: "Taking a blade of darbha grass from the mat and charging it with Brahmā's weapon, he blazed like the time-fire aimed at the bird."

sanskrit: cikṣepitha pradīptāṃ tām iṣīkāṃ vāyasaṃ prati anusṛṣṭas tadā kālo jagāma vividhāṃ gatim trāṇakāma imaṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ vai vicacāra ha
english: "You hurled that blazing reed at the crow; pursued, that bird moved through various courses in its desire for protection, ranging through all the worlds."

sanskrit: sa pitrā ca parityaktaḥ suraiḥ sarvair maharṣibhiḥ trīṃl lokān saṃparikramya tvām eva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: "Abandoned by its father, by all the gods, and by the great sages, having traversed the three worlds, it came to you alone for refuge."

sanskrit: taṃ tvaṃ nipatitaṃ bhūmau śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam vadhārham api kākutstha kṛpayā paryapālayaḥ na śarma labdhvā lokeṣu tvām eva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: "That one fallen to the ground, a refugee seeking shelter, though deserving of death, O Kākutstha, you protected out of compassion — for finding no safety in any of the worlds, it came to you alone for refuge."

sanskrit: paridyūnaṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ ca sa tvam āyāntam uktavān moghaṃ kartuṃ na śakyaṃ tu brāhmam astraṃ tad ucyatām
english: "To that one coming before you, dejected and despondent, you said: 'Brahmā's weapon cannot be made fruitless; let it be directed somewhere.'"

sanskrit: tatas tasyākṣi kākasya hinasti sma sa dakṣiṇam
english: "Then he struck out the right eye of that crow."

sanskrit: sa te tadā namaskṛtvā rājñe daśarathāya ca tvayā vīra visṛṣṭas tu pratipede svam ālayam
english: "He bowed to you then, and to King Daśaratha, and being released by you, O hero, returned to his own abode."

sanskrit: matkṛte kākamātre 'pi brahmāstraṃ samudīritam kasmād yo māṃ harat tvattaḥ kṣamase taṃ mahīpate
english: "For my sake Brahmā's weapon was invoked even for a mere crow; O lord of the earth, why do you tolerate him who robs me from you?"

sanskrit: sa kuruṣva mahotsāhaṃ kṛpāṃ mayi nararṣabha ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmas tvatta eva mayā śrutaḥ
english: "Show great energy, show compassion toward me, O bull among men — I have heard from you yourself that compassion is the highest dharma."

sanskrit: jānāmi tvāṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahotsāhaṃ mahābalam apārapāram akṣobhyaṃ gāmbhīryāt sāgaropamam bhartāraṃ sasamudrāyā dharaṇyā vāsavopamam
english: "I know you as one of great heroism, great energy, great strength, unfathomable in depth and unshakeable as the ocean, lord of the ocean-girdled earth, equal to Vāsava."

sanskrit: evam astravidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sattvavān balavān api kimartham astraṃ rakṣaḥsu na yojayasi rāghava
english: "Being thus the best knower of weapons, endowed with fortitude, and strong — why do you not employ your weapon against the rākṣasas, O Rāghava?"

sanskrit: na nāgā nāpi gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ rāmasya samare vegaṃ śaktāḥ prati samādhitum
english: "Neither the nāgas, nor the gandharvas, neither the asuras nor the hosts of Maruts are capable of withstanding Rāma's swiftness in battle."

sanskrit: tasyā vīryavataḥ kaś cid yady asti mayi saṃbhramaḥ kimarthaṃ na śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kṣayaṃ nayati rākṣasān
english: "If there is any concern for me in that valorous one, why does he not bring the rākṣasas to their end with sharp arrows?"

sanskrit: bhrātur ādeśam ādāya lakṣmaṇo vā paraṃtapaḥ kasya hetor na māṃ vīraḥ paritrāti mahābalaḥ
english: "Or Lakṣmaṇa the scorcher of foes — taking his brother's command, that hero of great strength — for what reason does he not rescue me?"

sanskrit: yadi tau puruṣavyāghrau vāyvindrasamatejasau surāṇām api durdharṣo kimarthaṃ mām upekṣataḥ
english: "If those two tigers among men are equal in energy to the wind and Indra, invincible even to the gods — why do they disregard me?"

sanskrit: mamaiva duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cin mahad asti na saṃśayaḥ samarthāv api tau yan māṃ nāvekṣete paraṃtapau
english: "There must be some great misdeed of mine, without doubt, since those two scorchers of foes, though capable, do not look to me."

sanskrit: kausalyā lokabhartāraṃ suṣuve yaṃ manasvinī taṃ mamārthe sukhaṃ pṛccha śirasā cābhivādaya
english: "The noble Kausalyā who bore him, the lord of the world — ask after his welfare on my behalf and salute him with a bow of the head."

sanskrit: srajaś ca sarvaratnāni priyā yāś ca varāṅganāḥ aiśvaryaṃ ca viśālāyāṃ pṛthivyām api durlabham
english: "Garlands, all gems, beloved noble women, and lordship over the broad earth, rare even for the great —"

sanskrit: pitaraṃ mātaraṃ caiva saṃmānyābhiprasādya ca anupravrajito rāmaṃ sumitrā yena suprajāḥ ānukūlyena dharmātmā tyaktvā sukham anuttamam
english: "— Sumitrā, mother of fine sons, having honored and propitiated both father and mother, and accompanied Rāma in going forth, through her dharmic-souled son who set aside unparalleled comfort —"

sanskrit: anugacchati kākutsthaṃ bhrātaraṃ pālayan vane siṃhaskandho mahābāhur manasvī priyadarśanaḥ
english: "— that lion-shouldered, mighty-armed, resolute, and handsome one follows Kākutstha his brother, protecting him in the forest."

sanskrit: pitṛvad vartate rāme mātṛvan māṃ samācaran hriyamāṇāṃ tadā vīro na tu māṃ veda lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "He behaves toward Rāma as a father, toward me as a mother; yet that hero Lakṣmaṇa did not know I was being carried off at that time."

sanskrit: vṛddhopasevī lakṣmīvān śakto na bahubhāṣitā rājaputraḥ priyaśreṣṭhaḥ sadṛśaḥ śvaśurasya me
english: "A servant of elders, glorious, capable, not one for many words, that prince is most dear, worthy of my father-in-law."

sanskrit: mattaḥ priyataro nityaṃ bhrātā rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ niyukto dhuri yasyāṃ tu tām udvahati vīryavān
english: "Rāma's brother Lakṣmaṇa is always dearer to him than I; whatever burden he is charged with, that valorous one carries it."

sanskrit: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavo naiva vṛddham āryam anusmarat sa mamārthāya kuśalaṃ vaktavyo vacanān mama mṛdur nityaṃ śucir dakṣaḥ priyo rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "Rāma, upon seeing him, never thinks even of the venerable and noble — tell him welfare on my behalf, at my word: gentle always, pure, skilled, dear to Rāma is Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: idaṃ brūyāś ca me nāthaṃ śūraṃ rāmaṃ punaḥ punaḥ jīvitaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi māsaṃ daśarathātmaja ūrdhvaṃ māsān na jīveyaṃ satyenāhaṃ bravīmi te
english: "And say this to my heroic lord Rāma again and again: 'I will sustain my life for one month, O son of Daśaratha; beyond that month I cannot live — I tell you this truthfully.'"

sanskrit: rāvaṇenoparuddhāṃ māṃ nikṛtyā pāpakarmaṇā trātum arhasi vīra tvaṃ pātālād iva kauśikīm
english: "Me, hemmed in by that evil-acting Rāvaṇa by cunning — you, O hero, should rescue as Kauśikī from the netherworld."

sanskrit: tato vastragataṃ muktvā divyaṃ cūḍāmaṇiṃ śubham pradeyo rāghavāyeti sītā hanumate dadau
english: Then Sītā, loosening from her garment the divine, beautiful cūḍāmaṇi crest-jewel, saying 'This is to be given to Rāghava,' gave it to Hanumān.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tato vīro maṇiratnam anuttamam aṅgulyā yojayām āsa na hy asyā prābhavad bhujaḥ
english: The hero, having received that peerless jewel-gem, placed it on his finger — for his arm could not match her form.

sanskrit: maṇiratnaṃ kapivaraḥ pratigṛhyābhivādya ca sītāṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā praṇataḥ pārśvataḥ sthitaḥ
english: The best of monkeys, having received the jewel-gem, paid his respects to Sītā, circumambulated her, and stood bowing at her side.

sanskrit: harṣeṇa mahatā yuktaḥ sītādarśanajena saḥ hṛdayena gato rāmaṃ śarīreṇa tu viṣṭhitaḥ
english: Filled with great joy born of the sight of Sītā, in his heart he had already gone to Rāma, though his body stood still.

sanskrit: maṇivaram upagṛhya taṃ mahārhaṃ janakanṛpātmajayā dhṛtaṃ prabhāvāt girivarapavanāvadhūtamuktaḥ sukhitamanāḥ pratisaṃkramaṃ prapede
english: Having taken up that supreme, most worthy jewel held by the daughter of King Janaka, freed by his power as one released by the wind stirring the king of mountains, with a joyful mind he set forth on his return journey.
